fields.statement: At aee97577 I read the diff from 3502ad9d: signoff.go adds ownerDeclared, checked after an existing sign-off and before the Autonomous branch, which reads the recorded stage autonomy (stage signoff, source workflow, mode owner) and falls back to the started definition's [autonomy] when the journal has no record; a setting-sourced owner is not a declaration. go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/run/ -run TestSignoff passed all 9, including TestSignoffWorkflowOwnerBeatsAutonomous (waits with SignoffWait, no signoff entry, then approve succeeds), TestSignoffAutoAndSettingSignOffAutonomously (workflow auto, setting auto, setting owner and a ship-only declaration each sign off under rule autonomous), TestSignoffOwnerFallsBackToDefinition (no record) and TestSignoffWorkflowOwnerChangesGoBack (request-changes goes back to review, then waits again on visit 2). go test -trimpath ./internal/run/... passed. go test -trimpath -count=1 ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/(run-signoff-workflow-owner|review-signoff-autonomous|workflow-stage-autonomy|run-autonomy-source) passed all four. The new script runs run start --autonomous on a workflow with [autonomy] signoff = owner and fake rex/claude, sees the log line naming the workflow's declaration, state stopped at signoff with signoff_waiting true and no rule autonomous sign-off, then rhiza run approve succeeds with rule owner. The other three scripts are unchanged in the diff
